guard: The fixed-group npm preflight refuses fallback access tokens and partial, incomplete, or stage-only releases before any registry write
why: A sequential recursive publish cannot recover after one package version lands and a later package refuses.
npm OIDC HTTP 201 proves identity, not the direct-publish Allowed action. These mutations remove one fail-before-write property at a time and every one must be killed by the fake registry smoke.
pnpm can continue after a failed OIDC exchange with an ambient npm access token. The preflight rejects every supported environment credential before its first registry or OIDC request.
